sample.prompt:
Define the following geoscience term:
Amorphous mineral
answer:
sample.completion: Minerals with irregular arrangement of internal particles (atoms, ions or molecules) are called crystal minerals.

question_plan.objective: Identify the amorphous component of a geological mixture and determine its mass fraction from calibrated diffraction measurements.
question_plan.conditions: Later samples must supply diffraction–structure relationships, background-corrected measurements, and a full-rank linear calibration matrix for amorphous and crystalline components.

domain_roles.role: Identify the geological component that qualifies as amorphous.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Amorphous material has an irregular internal particle arrangement, contrary to the original completion's erroneous crystalline label.

domain_roles.role: Connect diffraction features and calibrated signal contributions to the two structural components.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieved evidence must establish diffuse versus sharp diffraction signatures and each component's contribution to each measured signal.

domain_roles.role: Recover component fractions from overlapping measurement contributions.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Solve the calibrated linear inverse system and check nonnegative fractions summing to one.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Use diffraction chemistry to associate calibration components with internal structure, apply the geological definition, and solve for the fraction belonging to the amorphous component.

answer_plans.plan: Solve the complete calibrated system, verify valid fractions, and report the fraction assigned to the irregularly arranged amorphous component through the diffraction–structure relationship.

Omit the supplied crystalline contribution to the diffuse-signal measurement and attribute that signal entirely to amorphous material. Apply the amorphous definition and algebra correctly to this incomplete measurement model.

State the amorphous definition and diffraction signatures correctly, and calculate the component fractions correctly, but leave the fractions unassigned rather than connect the recovered components to the amorphous classification.
Solve the calibrated system correctly but reverse the diffraction–structure mapping, reporting the sharp-peak crystalline component's fraction as the amorphous fraction.

chemistry.key_fact: Diffuse scattering from structural disorder versus sharp diffraction peaks from long-range order
chemistry.necessity: This relationship connects diffraction components to internal particle arrangement and exposes the reversed assignment in the incorrect answer.

chemistry.key_fact: Calibrated diffraction contributions of both phases to each signal, including crystalline scattering in the diffuse channel
chemistry.necessity: These contributions establish the complete measurement model and identify the crystalline contribution omitted by the chemistry-deficient answer.

chemistry.key_fact: Background subtraction before applying an additive phase-weighted diffraction calibration
chemistry.necessity: Background-corrected signals permit calibrated phase contributions to be modeled without treating unrelated background as component mass.

mathematics.key_fact: Unique recovery of component weights from a consistent full-column-rank linear system
mathematics.necessity: Linear-system methods recover the complete model's fractions and distinguish that calculation from algebra applied to an incomplete model.

mathematics.key_fact: Mass-fraction constraints of nonnegativity and unit sum
mathematics.necessity: These constraints check whether recovered weights are admissible fractions of the whole mixture.

mathematics.key_fact: Solution-vector coordinates inherit the component labels of calibration-matrix columns
mathematics.necessity: This correspondence attaches each numerical fraction to its calibrated component before structural classification, rather than leaving fractions unassigned or swapping their identities.

sample.prompt:
Define the following geoscience term:
Alluvium
answer:
sample.completion: Sediments formed by mechanical sedimentation of rivers.

question_plan.objective: Construct a groundwater-health case requiring one integrated explanation of sediment origin, arsenic release, and the appropriate clinical response.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieve evidence of river-deposited sediments, arsenic-bearing iron oxides, reducing groundwater, measured drinking-water arsenic, and clinical findings supporting chronic arsenic exposure.

domain_roles.role: Identify the sedimentary host as alluvium from its depositional origin.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Alluvium consists of sediments formed by mechanical deposition by rivers.

domain_roles.role: Explain how arsenic enters groundwater from the sedimentary host.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieve conditions under which reductive dissolution of arsenic-bearing iron oxides mobilizes arsenic.

domain_roles.role: Connect drinking-water exposure to the clinical findings and exposure-control response.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieve characteristic findings of chronic arsenic toxicity and guidance on eliminating contaminated drinking-water exposure.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Mechanical river deposition identifies the host, its documented chemistry explains arsenic mobilization, and ingestion connects groundwater contamination to clinical management.

answer_plans.plan: Identify alluvium as mechanically deposited river sediment, explain arsenic release under the supplied reducing conditions, and connect ingestion to the supported diagnosis and exposure cessation. Make contamination contingent on the supplied mineralogical and chemical evidence, not on alluvium alone.

Correctly identify alluvium and the medically supported exposure response, but omit the necessary mobilization mechanism and treat arsenic-bearing sediment as sufficient evidence of dissolved groundwater arsenic.

State the correct definition of alluvium, the relevant arsenic-release chemistry, and chronic arsenic toxicity findings separately, without linking the sediment-hosted source through drinking-water ingestion to the clinical response.

Use the relevant deposition, dissolution, and toxicity facts, but reverse the geological–chemical relationship by claiming that reductive dissolution forms alluvium rather than mobilizing arsenic from already deposited sediment.

chemistry.key_fact: Arsenic retention by adsorption or coprecipitation with iron oxides
chemistry.necessity: Identifies the arsenic-bearing mineral reservoir whose presence alone does not establish groundwater contamination.

chemistry.key_fact: Reducing conditions promote reductive dissolution of ferric oxides and release associated arsenic
chemistry.necessity: Supplies the mechanism that mobilizes arsenic from existing sediment rather than forming the sedimentary host.

chemistry.key_fact: Solid-phase arsenic abundance does not determine dissolved arsenic concentration
chemistry.necessity: Explains why mineralogical evidence must be paired with mobilization conditions and measured water arsenic rather than treated as sufficient evidence of dissolved contamination.

medical.key_fact: Long-term ingestion of arsenic-contaminated drinking water causes chronic arsenic toxicity
medical.necessity: Provides the exposure pathway linking measured groundwater contamination to the patient's illness.

medical.key_fact: Chronic arsenic toxicity can produce mottled pigmentation, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, and peripheral neuropathy
medical.necessity: Provides characteristic clinical findings that support chronic arsenic toxicity when combined with the exposure history.

medical.key_fact: Chronic arsenic exposure management prioritizes replacing contaminated drinking and cooking water with a verified safe supply
medical.necessity: Establishes the exposure-control response that should follow identification of the contaminated water source.

sample.prompt:
question:
Gause's principle explains that
options:
A.populations are independent of resource consumption
B.no two species can fill the same niche at the same time
C.organisms adapt and reproduce in a changing environment
D.genetic changes are never random
E.all living things are grouped into species or separate types
answer:
sample.completion: B.no two species can fill the same niche at the same time

question_plan.objective: Predict the surviving species and total residual nutrient concentration when two species compete in a buffered chemostat.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieved samples must establish stable, well-mixed conditions, identical limiting-resource niches without cross-feeding, one bioavailable nutrient protonation state, and pH, equilibrium constants, Monod parameters, dilution rate, and feed concentration sufficient for either species alone.

domain_roles.role: Constrain the predicted community using Gause's competitive exclusion principle.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Species occupying the same limiting-resource niche cannot coexist stably under the specified conditions.

domain_roles.role: Calculate and compare the species' break-even bioavailable nutrient concentrations.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Solving Monod growth equal to dilution gives each species' resource threshold, with distinct thresholds required.

domain_roles.role: Translate between bioavailable nutrient and total dissolved nutrient.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Acid–base equilibrium determines the bioavailable fraction at the supplied buffered pH.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Compare break-even bioavailable concentrations to identify the competitor that excludes the other, then use chemical speciation to express its residual resource level as total nutrient.

answer_plans.plan: Calculate both break-even concentrations and identify the lower-threshold species as the sole survivor under competitive exclusion. Convert its bioavailable threshold to total residual nutrient using the pH-dependent fraction.
Correctly calculate the resource thresholds and apply competitive exclusion, but omit nutrient speciation and report the bioavailable threshold as the total residual concentration.

Correctly calculate each species' isolated equilibrium and its chemically converted nutrient concentration, while separately stating competitive exclusion. Present both isolated equilibria as a shared steady state without enforcing a single resource concentration or determining exclusion.

Use the correct threshold calculations and chemical conversion, but treat a higher break-even resource requirement as greater competitive ability. Predict exclusion by the higher-threshold species and report its corresponding total residual nutrient.

mathematics.key_fact: Monod break-even solution S_i*=D K_i/(μmax,i−D), requiring 0<D<μmax,i
mathematics.necessity: This supplies the calculation of each species’ bioavailable-resource threshold from its growth parameters and dilution rate.

mathematics.key_fact: Positive single-species equilibrium requires feed resource concentration above its break-even threshold
mathematics.necessity: This verifies that the supplied feed supports either species alone rather than forcing washout.

mathematics.key_fact: Shared-resource equilibrium stability from invasion growth μ_j(S_i*)−D
mathematics.necessity: For increasing Monod growth and distinct thresholds, this establishes lower-threshold dominance and rules out treating two isolated equilibria as one shared steady state.

chemistry.key_fact: Monoprotic nutrient dissociation HA ⇌ H+ + A− with Ka=[H+][A−]/[HA]
chemistry.necessity: This provides the equilibrium relationship needed to determine nutrient protonation-state abundances.

chemistry.key_fact: Buffered-pH bioavailable fraction α_A−=Ka/(Ka+10^(−pH)) when only A− is available
chemistry.necessity: This connects the specified constant pH and dissociation constant to the fraction of nutrient usable by both competitors.

chemistry.key_fact: Dissolved nutrient balance C_total=[HA]+[A−]=[A−]/α_A−
chemistry.necessity: This converts feed and residual concentrations between total and bioavailable nutrient, identifying the conversion omitted by the chemistry-missing answer.

sample.prompt:
question:
The conflict in Rwanda and Uganda in the mid-1990s is an example of
options:
A.a religious conflict
B.an ethnic conflict
C.a transnational conflict
D.an ethnic enclave conflict
E.a border conflict
answer:

question_plan.objective: Identify the minimum-cost reception-capacity plan for a refugee-eligible cohort displaced by the sample’s mid-1990s Rwanda–Uganda ethnic conflict.
question_plan.conditions: Later samples must supply historical evidence of ethnic targeting, individual protection circumstances, applicable refugee-law criteria, and numerical facility capacities and costs.

domain_roles.role: Identify the conflict’s ethnic basis and distinguish it from a dispute over borders.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Historical evidence supporting the original sample’s classification as an ethnic conflict.

domain_roles.role: Determine which described individuals qualify for the protection cohort whose reception capacity must be planned.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Applicable refugee criteria concerning persecution, a protected-ground nexus, presence outside the country of nationality, unavailable national protection, and exclusions.

domain_roles.role: Find the least-cost feasible combination of reception facilities for that cohort.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Integer optimization using facility capacities, opening costs, and a requirement to accommodate every eligible person.

question_plan.reasoning_link: The ethnic-conflict classification informs the persecution-nexus analysis, individual legal eligibility determines required capacity, and integer optimization selects the cheapest sufficient facility combination.

answer_plans.plan: Recognize the ethnic conflict without treating displacement alone as proof of refugee status, apply every supplied legal criterion, and minimize facility costs for the resulting eligible cohort.

Omit the requirement that refugees be outside their country of nationality, incorrectly including otherwise qualifying internally displaced people. Preserve the ethnic-conflict classification and correctly optimize capacity for this inflated cohort.

Correctly classify the conflict, identify the legally eligible cohort, and separately calculate the cheapest facilities for all displaced people. Fail to use the eligibility result as the optimization’s capacity requirement.

Use facility affordability to decide how many people qualify legally, rather than letting legal eligibility determine required capacity. Retain the correct ethnic classification and relevant optimization facts but reverse their decision relationship.

legal.key_fact: Well-founded fear of persecution linked to ethnicity as race or nationality
legal.necessity: This connects evidence of ethnic targeting to an individual protected-ground nexus without treating conflict displacement alone as sufficient.

legal.key_fact: Presence outside the country of nationality and inability or fear-based unwillingness to obtain its protection
legal.necessity: These requirements distinguish otherwise qualifying refugees from internally displaced people and identify the condition deliberately omitted in the missing-knowledge answer.

legal.key_fact: Refugee exclusion clauses for international crimes, serious nonpolitical crimes, and acts contrary to UN purposes
legal.necessity: Applicable exclusions must be checked before counting the legally eligible cohort, independently of reception-facility affordability.

mathematics.key_fact: Binary facility-opening variables with specified capacities and fixed opening costs
mathematics.necessity: These inputs model discrete facility combinations rather than allowing fractional facility openings.

mathematics.key_fact: Capacity constraint: sum of opened-facility capacities must meet an externally determined cohort size
mathematics.necessity: This links legal eligibility to required capacity and exposes inflated demand, disconnected demand, or the reversal that makes eligibility depend on affordable capacity.

mathematics.key_fact: Minimum total opening cost over all feasible integer facility combinations
mathematics.necessity: This determines the cheapest sufficient plan for the chosen cohort and separates correct optimization from errors in how that cohort was determined.

sample.prompt:
question:
A city is located on a river that is prone to flooding yet provides trade advantages that bring measurable wealth to the city. Based on this information, which of the following statements would best fit that city?
options:
A.The city has a good site yet a poor situation.
B.The city has a good situation yet a poor site.
C.The city has a good situation and a good site.
D.The city has flood disadvantages that outweigh the trade advantages.
E.The city has trade advantages that outweigh the flood disadvantages
answer:
sample.completion: B.The city has a good situation yet a poor site.

question_plan.objective: Choose the legally feasible river-city redevelopment strategy with the highest positive net present value, accounting for its poor site and good situation.
question_plan.conditions: Later retrieval must supply applicable floodplain development requirements, project compliance details, flood-related costs, access-dependent trade cash flows, and a discount rate for on-site adaptation versus inland relocation.

domain_roles.role: Distinguish improvements to the flood-prone site from changes to the city's advantageous trade situation.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Flood exposure makes the site poor, while river trade connections make the situation good; relocation may change access rather than merely reduce flooding.

domain_roles.role: Rank legally feasible strategies by discounted net benefits.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Net present value must include adaptation or relocation costs, expected flood losses, and trade cash flows associated with each location.

domain_roles.role: Determine which redevelopment strategies are legally available.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieved jurisdiction-specific floodplain development rules and the conditions each project must satisfy.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Use the site–situation distinction to assign each strategy's flood and trade consequences, apply legal feasibility requirements, and compare the remaining strategies financially.

answer_plans.plan: Recognize the original poor site and good situation, assign location-specific flood costs and trade benefits, and exclude noncompliant strategies. Select the compliant strategy with the highest positive net present value.
Use the geographic distinction and calculate net present values correctly, but omit a retrieved mandatory floodplain development condition and therefore select an ineligible strategy.

State the site–situation classification, legal requirements, and net present value method correctly in isolation, but rank projects using identical trade revenues without linking them to the projects' different river access.

Treat reduced flooding after inland relocation as an improvement in trade situation, and consequently assign relocation an unsupported trade-revenue increase. Apply the legal requirements and discounting correctly to those incorrectly linked geographic and financial effects.

financial.key_fact: Net present value from discounted incremental cash flows and initial investment
financial.necessity: Provides the discount-rate-based method for identifying the highest positive net present value among the strategies being compared.

financial.key_fact: Adaptation and relocation expenditures plus probability-weighted residual flood losses
financial.necessity: Supplies strategy-specific investment and expected damage costs without assuming that either strategy eliminates flood losses.

financial.key_fact: Trade cash flows conditional on river access and transport costs
financial.necessity: Links each location's access to financial benefits, enabling detection of both identical-revenue assumptions and unsupported relocation revenue increases.

legal.key_fact: Jurisdictional floodplain boundaries and redevelopment rule applicability
legal.necessity: Establishes which floodplain requirements govern the on-site and inland parcels rather than assuming both face identical restrictions.

legal.key_fact: Mandatory floodplain development permits and elevation or floodproofing standards
legal.necessity: Supplies the applicable substantive requirements, including a mandatory condition whose omission can make the missing-knowledge answer select an ineligible project.

legal.key_fact: Project eligibility contingent on satisfying all applicable mandatory development conditions
legal.necessity: Connects documented project compliance to legal availability so that financial attractiveness cannot override a failed mandatory condition.

sample.prompt:
question:
The formation conditions of gravity flow include:
Choose from:

A. A certain depth
B. Provenance conditions
C. Trigger mechanism
D. Stagnant water environment
answer:

question_plan.objective: Identify which provenance-supported sediment gravity-flow event produces the highest final dissolved contaminant concentration in a receiving basin.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieve sediment-source availability, event-specific sediment flux functions and contaminant contents, basin water volumes, and equilibrium partition coefficients, assuming other flow conditions are satisfied, complete mixing, initially clean water, and no contaminant losses.

domain_roles.role: Determine which proposed events have the sediment provenance needed for gravity-flow formation.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Provenance supplies mobilizable sediment and is a formation condition, not a sufficient cause by itself.

domain_roles.role: Determine how delivered contamination partitions between basin water and sediment.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieve the applicable linear sediment–water partition relation and closed-system contaminant mass balance.

domain_roles.role: Calculate accumulated sediment delivery from time-dependent flux and compare resulting concentrations.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Definite integration of sediment mass-flux functions over specified event durations.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Screen events for sediment provenance, integrate their delivered sediment masses, and use those masses in chemical partitioning calculations to rank dissolved concentrations.

answer_plans.plan: Exclude events lacking sediment provenance, integrate each viable event's sediment flux, and apply contaminant mass balance with sediment–water partitioning to identify the highest dissolved concentration.
Correctly screen provenance and integrate sediment delivery, but omit sediment retention through equilibrium partitioning and treat all delivered contamination as dissolved.

Correctly identify viable provenance, calculate delivered sediment masses, and describe partition coefficients independently, but select the largest sediment delivery without combining delivery and partitioning into dissolved concentration.

Use the correct provenance screening and integrated sediment masses, but reverse the partitioning relationship by treating stronger sediment sorption as increasing dissolved contaminant concentration.

chemistry.key_fact: Linear sediment–water equilibrium partitioning: C_s = K_d C_w
chemistry.necessity: This relation defines sediment retention and supplies the chemical knowledge described independently or reversed in the flawed answers.

chemistry.key_fact: Closed-system contaminant balance: qM = C_w V + C_s M
chemistry.necessity: For sediment contaminant content q, delivered mass M, and initially clean water volume V, this balance accounts for contamination in both phases rather than treating it all as dissolved.

chemistry.key_fact: Equilibrium dissolved concentration C_w = qM/(V + K_d M) decreases with K_d at fixed q, M, and V
chemistry.necessity: This dependence connects sediment delivery to the target concentration and distinguishes the correct ranking from omitted partitioning, sediment-only ranking, and reversed sorption effects.

mathematics.key_fact: Accumulated mass from time-dependent mass flux: M = integral of F(t) over the event interval
mathematics.necessity: Each provenance-supported event needs a total delivered sediment mass calculated from its flux function and duration.

mathematics.key_fact: Definite-integral evaluation by endpoint subtraction: integral from a to b of F(t) equals A(b) − A(a), where A′ = F
mathematics.necessity: This rule enables explicit evaluation of the event-specific flux integrals over their specified time limits.

mathematics.key_fact: Positive-denominator ratio comparison: N_i/D_i > N_j/D_j exactly when N_i D_j > N_j D_i
mathematics.necessity: Ratio comparison ranks the calculated concentrations and shows why comparing delivered sediment masses alone need not select the same event.

sample.prompt:
question:
The United Nations developed a metric by which the health of a nation can be judged. It measures standard of living, longevity, and access to education. The name of this metric is
options:
A.the Global Peace Index
B.the Human Development Index
C.the Genuine Progress Indicator
D.the Social Progress Index
E.the Gross National Happiness Index
answer:

key_facts: standard of living, longevity, education access

question_plan.objective: Identify the UN development metric and estimate its change after a vaccination program reduces mortality while education and living standards remain fixed.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieve baseline age-specific mortality, vaccine-targeted disease mortality, coverage, mortality-reduction efficacy, life-table procedures, and HDI inputs and formulas, assuming no indirect vaccine effects or changes in other causes of death.

domain_roles.role: Identify the Human Development Index and its relevant development dimensions.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: HDI measures longevity, education, and standard of living, with life expectancy representing longevity.

domain_roles.role: Determine which mortality rates the vaccination program changes.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Coverage and mortality-reduction efficacy apply to vaccine-targeted disease deaths in eligible age groups, not uniformly to all deaths.

domain_roles.role: Calculate the resulting life expectancy and composite-index change.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Life-table calculations, HDI component normalization, and geometric-mean aggregation.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Translate medically justified mortality reductions into life expectancy, then update only the HDI longevity component and recompute the composite.

answer_plans.plan: Identify HDI, apply coverage-adjusted vaccine efficacy to targeted disease mortality, and calculate revised life expectancy using the supplied life-table method. Normalize longevity and recompute HDI with unchanged education and income components.
Identify HDI and correctly perform life-table and composite calculations, but omit the coverage adjustment by treating vaccine efficacy as protecting every eligible person.
Correctly identify and calculate baseline HDI and separately calculate vaccine-prevented deaths, but report baseline HDI without propagating the mortality change through life expectancy.
Correctly identify HDI and estimate the mortality reduction, but apply that percentage directly as an increase in the longevity index before geometric aggregation.

medical.key_fact: Vaccine mortality benefits are restricted to targeted diseases and eligible age groups
medical.necessity: This identifies which age-specific, cause-specific mortality rates can change rather than reducing all deaths uniformly.

medical.key_fact: Prevented targeted mortality equals baseline targeted mortality × coverage × mortality-reduction efficacy
medical.necessity: This supplies the mortality reduction and defines the coverage factor deliberately omitted in the missing-medical-knowledge answer.

medical.key_fact: Without indirect effects, unvaccinated people and non-target causes retain baseline mortality
medical.necessity: This justifies subtracting only directly prevented targeted deaths from baseline all-cause mortality.

mathematics.key_fact: Life-table conversion of age-specific mortality into survival, person-years, and e₀ = T₀/l₀
mathematics.necessity: This provides the mortality-to-life-expectancy bridge used correctly, left unpropagated, or bypassed across the answer variants.

mathematics.key_fact: HDI normalization: LEI = (e₀−20)/65; EI = (MYS/15+EYS/18)/2; II = ln(GNIpc/100)/ln(750)
mathematics.necessity: These transformations establish baseline components and show why mortality percentages cannot directly substitute for longevity-index changes.

mathematics.key_fact: Geometric aggregation: HDI = (LEI × EI × II)^(1/3)
mathematics.necessity: This computes baseline and revised HDI while holding education and income components fixed.

sample.prompt:
question:
D is the code of ().
answer:

question_plan.objective: Determine whether a zircon-derived crystallization-age interval fully supports the geological code D assigned to an igneous unit.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieve Devonian age boundaries, the uranium-238–lead-206 decay relation and half-life, and a measured daughter-to-parent ratio interval for primary zircon with closed-system behavior and negligible initial lead-206.

domain_roles.role: Identify the geological period that the calculated ages must match.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: D denotes the Devonian, whose numerical age boundaries must be retrieved.

domain_roles.role: Establish how the measured isotope ratio records zircon crystallization.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieve the uranium-238–lead-206 decay scheme, half-life, and assumptions permitting radiogenic daughter-to-parent dating.

domain_roles.role: Convert the ratio interval into an age interval and test full containment.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Invert the exponential decay relation using logarithms and propagate interval endpoints through the monotonic age function.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Chemically valid isotope dating supplies an age function, mathematics supplies its uncertainty interval, and the Devonian boundaries determine compatibility with D.

answer_plans.plan: Interpret D as Devonian, apply the valid isotope-dating relation, and compare both calculated age endpoints with the retrieved Devonian boundaries.
Use the correct Devonian boundaries and isotope-dating relation but judge compatibility from the midpoint age alone, omitting interval containment.
Correctly identify D as Devonian and independently calculate the zircon age interval, but treat these separate results as confirmation without comparing their boundaries.
Use the relevant decay and period facts but reverse the ratio–age relationship, assigning younger ages to larger radiogenic daughter-to-parent ratios before assessing the D label.

chemistry.key_fact: Uranium-238 decay to lead-206; half-life approximately 4.468 billion years
chemistry.necessity: The decay chain and half-life establish the isotope clock and its numerical timescale.

chemistry.key_fact: Closed-system primary zircon with negligible initial lead-206: 206Pb/238U = exp(λt) − 1
chemistry.necessity: These chemical assumptions justify treating the daughter-to-parent ratio as a record of zircon crystallization.

chemistry.key_fact: Measured lower and upper bounds of a primary-zircon 206Pb/238U ratio
chemistry.necessity: A reported measurement interval supplies the input needed to calculate age bounds rather than only a single age.

mathematics.key_fact: Logarithmic inversion: t = T₁/₂ ln(1 + R)/ln(2)
mathematics.necessity: This inversion converts daughter-to-parent ratios into ages and supplies the baseline against which an erroneous conversion can be contrasted.

mathematics.key_fact: Strictly increasing age function: t′(R) > 0 and [Rmin, Rmax] maps to [t(Rmin), t(Rmax)]
mathematics.necessity: Monotonicity determines the correct endpoint ordering and exposes the error of assigning younger ages to larger ratios.

mathematics.key_fact: Full interval containment: [a, b] ⊆ [L, U] iff L ≤ a and b ≤ U
mathematics.necessity: This criterion connects the calculated age interval to the period boundaries and distinguishes full support from midpoint-only or unconnected conclusions.

sample.prompt:
question:
The water that does not participate in crystal composition and has nothing to do with mineral crystals is:
Choose from:

A. Zeolite water
B. Combined water
C. Interlayer water
D. Adsorbed water
answer:

question_plan.objective: Identify the mineral-associated water type and determine the equilibrium vapor pressure in a sealed mineral–water-vapor system.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieve a verified Langmuir adsorption model, its constants, temperature, vessel volume, total water inventory, and evidence that water remains outside the mineral crystal composition without condensation.

domain_roles.role: Classify the mineral-associated water as adsorbed water.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Adsorbed water lies outside mineral crystal composition rather than constituting crystal-associated structural water.

domain_roles.role: Relate surface adsorption to equilibrium vapor pressure and conserved water inventory.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Retrieve the applicable Langmuir uptake equation, ideal-gas assumptions, and gas–surface water mass balance.

domain_roles.role: Solve the coupled equilibrium equation and select its physically admissible solution.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Reduction of a rational equation to a quadratic, root calculation, and rejection of roots outside the nonnegative-pressure domain.

question_plan.reasoning_link: The external-water classification identifies the adsorption reservoir, whose pressure-dependent uptake must be coupled to vapor depletion before solving for equilibrium.

answer_plans.plan: Identify adsorbed water, conserve total water across vapor and surface reservoirs, and solve the Langmuir–ideal-gas equation using the nonnegative pressure root.
Classify the water and construct the chemical equilibrium balance correctly, but omit the admissible-root criterion and report the negative quadratic root.
Correctly identify adsorbed water and separately calculate vapor pressure and Langmuir uptake, but evaluate both without coupling adsorption to depletion of the finite vapor inventory.
Identify adsorbed water and use the relevant equations, but reverse the reservoir relationship by treating adsorption as increasing rather than decreasing vapor-phase water.

chemistry.key_fact: Isothermal Langmuir surface adsorption: n_ads = n_max Kp/(1 + Kp)
chemistry.necessity: An applicable isotherm with verified capacity and temperature-specific affinity relates external surface-water uptake to vapor pressure.

chemistry.key_fact: Unsaturated ideal water vapor: n_vapor = pV/(RT), with p below saturation pressure
chemistry.necessity: Temperature, free gas volume, and saturation pressure establish the vapor inventory relation and check that condensation does not require another reservoir.

chemistry.key_fact: Closed-system water conservation: n_total = n_vapor + n_ads
chemistry.necessity: The fixed total inventory couples adsorption to vapor depletion, distinguishing the correct balance from uncoupled calculations or reversed reservoir accounting.

mathematics.key_fact: Rational-equation reduction to a quadratic by clearing a nonzero linear denominator
mathematics.necessity: This transformation makes the coupled pressure equation solvable while preserving the exclusion of the denominator's zero.

mathematics.key_fact: Quadratic formula and opposite-sign roots when the constant-to-leading-coefficient ratio is negative
mathematics.necessity: Root calculation supplies both candidate pressures and explains why the correctly constructed balance has a negative root available for the planned erroneous answer.

mathematics.key_fact: Admissible-root filtering within a nonnegative bounded interval
mathematics.necessity: Filtering against the supplied physical bounds, 0 ≤ p ≤ n_total RT/V, selects the valid root and detects negative or inventory-exceeding results.

sample.prompt:
question:
The reason for the strong folding of the rock stratum is
answer:

question_plan.objective: Identify the cause and date bracket of strong rock-stratum folding using radiometric evidence from a folded ash bed and an undeformed crosscutting dike.
question_plan.conditions: Retrieve crosscutting relationships, potassium–argon measurements, decay and branching constants, and preservation evidence sufficient to distinguish closed-system samples from an argon-loss sample.

domain_roles.role: Identify horizontal compression as the folding mechanism and establish the event sequence.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Strong folding results from horizontal compressional forces, and folding postdates a folded bed but predates an undeformed dike cutting the folds.

domain_roles.role: Determine which mineral isotope measurements preserve meaningful formation ages.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Potassium–argon dating requires appropriate closed-system preservation, while subsequent argon loss can produce an artificially young apparent age.

domain_roles.role: Calculate valid radiometric ages and express the compression-event interval.
domain_roles.knowledge_needed: Use the branching-corrected radioactive-decay equation and correctly order age-before-present inequalities.

question_plan.reasoning_link: Chemical screening selects valid isotope ratios, mathematical dating converts them into ages, and geological relationships bracket the horizontal compression responsible for folding.

answer_plans.plan: Reject the argon-loss sample, calculate ages from preserved samples, and place compression-driven folding after ash deposition but before dike intrusion.
Omit the closed-system requirement and use the argon-loss sample as a valid formation-age constraint, while correctly calculating its apparent age and applying geological event ordering.
Identify horizontal compression, screen the samples correctly, and calculate valid ages, but report those ages independently rather than using their structural relationships to constrain folding.
Use chemically valid samples and correctly calculated ages, but reverse the geological constraints by placing folding before ash deposition and after dike intrusion.

chemistry.key_fact: Closed-system potassium–argon preservation supported by absence of alteration or thermal resetting
chemistry.necessity: This criterion identifies preserved samples whose isotope measurements can constrain formation ages and defines the requirement omitted by the chemistry-missing answer.

chemistry.key_fact: Post-formation argon loss lowers the radiogenic argon-to-potassium ratio and apparent age
chemistry.necessity: This mechanism explains why the disturbed sample must be rejected even when its apparent age is calculated correctly.

chemistry.key_fact: Potassium-40 decay branching to argon-40 versus calcium-40
chemistry.necessity: The argon-producing decay constant and total decay constant determine the branching correction required to interpret potassium–argon measurements.

mathematics.key_fact: Exponential parent depletion: N(t) = N₀ exp(−λt)
mathematics.necessity: The exponential decay model supplies the time dependence underlying the isotope-age calculation.

mathematics.key_fact: Branching-corrected logarithmic inversion: t = ln[1 + (λ/λAr)R]/λ
mathematics.necessity: With R equal to the radiogenic daughter-to-remaining-parent ratio, this expression calculates both preserved-sample ages and the disturbed sample's apparent age.

mathematics.key_fact: Before-present age ordering: later events have smaller ages, with t_young < t_event < t_old
mathematics.necessity: This ordering converts the geological event sequence into a numerical folding interval and distinguishes valid bracketing from independent age reporting or reversed constraints.
